findings.description: Critical: D2 requires the workspace state lock to be released across approval-service I/O (spec 'Same-generation routing is concurrency safe' -> 'approval-service waiting does not hold the workspace state lock'; task 1.4 requires an unrelated workspace transition to remain available during a blocked coordinator wait), but the decision-persistence path it routes through is a whole-file, read-modify-write of the SAME file that holds dispatch_attempts, taken from a snapshot read BEFORE the wait. `gate_router.evaluate` loads the checkpoint at gate_router.py:398, then blocks inside `service.evaluate` for the full notify_with_timeout window (approval_gate.py polls with `self.sleep` until timeout), then persists at gate_router.py:442 via `CheckpointManager.record_gate_decision` -> `save` -> `models.save_checkpoint`, which writes `checkpoint.to_dict()` wholesale (checkpoint.py:55-62, 98-123; models.py:1137-1153). Any durable transition another host task commits under `execution._state_lock` during that window (child_start's generation CAS, acknowledge, enter, a second batch's apply) is reverted when routing's decision is written; conversely, `ExecutionAdapter.apply` — which itself holds the workspace lock across the replan_required gate window at orchestrator.py:1095-1108 — will later save its own pre-route snapshot and silently drop the gate_decisions record that routing just wrote, leaving a mirror pending entry whose `decision_id` resolves to nothing and making `require_approval_ref` reject a proceed that was really granted. The reverted-claim case is durably corrupting: the attempt reverts to `prepared` while its exclusive launch marker still exists on disk, so `_write_marker_exclusive`'s O_EXCL create (execution.py:262-283) fails on every subsequent claim and the dispatch can never be re-launched. No decision, task, or test in the plan closes this: the plan adds only a gate-subject lock, which does not serialize against workspace transitions at all.
findings.resolution: Add a decision to D2 requiring that gate-decision persistence (and the mirror projection that follows it) re-read durable state under the workspace state lock immediately before writing, rather than saving a snapshot captured before approval I/O — e.g. make the persist step take `execution._state_lock` (lazily imported, matching the existing cycle_state lazy-import convention), reload the checkpoint, append the record, and save; or make `CheckpointManager.record_gate_decision` merge the record into the on-disk JSON instead of overwriting from the in-memory dataclass. Add a RED test (extend task 1.4) that commits an unrelated `child_start`/`acknowledge` transition during a blocked coordinator wait and asserts it is still durable after the decision is recorded, and a second that asserts the routed decision survives a concurrent `apply` on another batch. If the merge lands in `skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/checkpoint.py`, add that path to wp-escalation-routing `locks.files` and `scope.write_allow`, which currently allow only execution.py, gate_router.py, cycle_state.py, SKILL.md, tests, and the gate-decision schema.

findings.description: Critical: D7 and the spec scenario 'Auto posture resumes a fresh application generation' assert that clearing the generation-G `application_journal` is sufficient for the resumed generation to 'start, acknowledge, enter, and apply a fresh journal', but for any batch with more than one member that apply call cannot be made under the plan's own constraints. `resume` preserves the dispatch ID (execution.py:857-906), dispatch IDs are `{batch_id}:{item_id}:attempt-N` (orchestrator.py:320-324), and `_batch_attempts` selects every attempt with that batch prefix, so the resumed member stays in its original batch. `apply_delegated_batch` then rejects any call whose result set is not exactly the whole batch ('result membership mismatch for delegated batch', orchestrator.py:636-638), and `ExecutionAdapter.apply` is frozen unchanged by D1/the contract note, so the natural implementation — apply the resumed member's new result alone — always raises. Re-submitting the whole batch is not a safe fallback either: `execution.apply` re-runs `_validate_exact_evidence` for every success/parked member (execution.py:930-931, 961-1003), which re-resolves each sibling's worktree, branch, HEAD commit, and loop-state digest, so an already-completed sibling whose worktree was torn down, merged, or advanced after completion makes the resumed member's apply permanently unappliable. The plan's only end-to-end proof (task 1.2, test 6) is single-member, so this never surfaces in the specified test set, while task 3.4's documentation guards and task 3.1's protocol update say nothing about post-resume batch membership.
findings.resolution: State the post-resume apply protocol explicitly in D7 and in the SKILL.md collect/apply protocol (task 3.1): whether the host must re-submit the full batch membership with each already-applied member's byte-identical prior result (and how sibling evidence revalidation is expected to survive worktree teardown), or whether a resumed generation is applied through a different seam. Add a RED test under task 1.2 that parks one member of a two-member batch, resumes it, and applies its fresh generation-G+1 result while the sibling is already `effects_applied` — including the case where the sibling's worktree is no longer resolvable — and pin the chosen rule with a documentation guard in task 3.4.
